description.short_caption: Peripheral smear, Wright-Giemsa stain, showing intracellular inclusions.
description.detailed_description: This is a high-magnification image of a peripheral blood smear stained with Wright-Giemsa. Numerous red blood cells are visible, appearing as round, pale pink discs with central pallor. A few cells contain small, dark purple intracellular inclusions, consistent with parasitic organisms. The background is clear, with no significant debris or artifacts.
visible_findings: red blood cells with central pallor

description.short_caption: Peripheral smear showing intraerythrocytic inclusions, Wright-Giemsa stain, x1250 magnification.
description.detailed_description: This is a high-magnification image of a peripheral blood smear stained with Wright-Giemsa. Numerous red blood cells (RBCs) are visible, appearing as round, pale-pink structures with central pallor. Several RBCs contain small, dark-blue intraerythrocytic inclusions consistent with parasitic forms. The inclusions are suggestive of a protozoal infection, such as Plasmodium species or Babesia species. The background is clear, with no significant leukocytes or platelets visible.
visible_findings: round red blood cells with central pallor
absence of significant leukocytes or platelets

description.short_caption: Peripheral smear, Wright-Giemsa stain, showing intracellular inclusion.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a peripheral blood smear stained with Wright-Giemsa at high magnification (approximately x1250). Numerous red blood cells (RBCs) are visible, appearing as round, pale pink structures with central pallor. One RBC contains a distinct intracellular inclusion, which is darkly stained and suggestive of a parasitic organism. The background is clear, and no significant leukocytes or platelets are prominently visible.
visible_findings: round red blood cells with central pallor

description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing the thorax, including bilateral lung fields, mediastinal structures, and bony thoracic anatomy. The lung fields appear clear without obvious consolidation, pleural effusion, or masses. The cardiac silhouette is within normal limits, and there is no visible evidence of pneumothorax. The bony structures, including ribs, clavicles, and spine, appear intact without fractures or deformities.
